analysis: The experiment cleanly contradicts the stated hypothesis. The candidate reduced standalone primary by 0.00904 versus the incumbent, with a paired 95% CI of [-0.01138, -0.00721], excluding zero. Both component metrics were low enough to produce a primary mean of 0.59494, and the result was stable across three seeds (seed SD 0.00023). The predicted short-history benefit also did not occur: the lowest-history quartile declined by 0.00627, while every history quartile, item-popularity quartile, and tab slice was negative. Losses were somewhat smaller for the shortest-history users than for longer-history users, but this is only a relative pattern within an overall degradation and does not support the claim. The branch also failed as an error diversifier: adding it to the portfolio changed primary by -0.000253, with a CI crossing zero, so there is no evidence of complementary value. Assuming the contract diagnostics confirmed uniform same-user sampling, these results reject fixed eight-pair macro-user balancing in this three-epoch custom FM configuration; they do not establish that all forms of user-balanced weighting are harmful, because the intervention also sharply capped information use and changed the trainer implementation relative to the parent.
next_lesson: Do not replace exposure-weighted FM training with a hard eight-pair-per-user cap; if revisiting macro alignment, preserve substantially more within-user information and isolate weighting from trainer changes.
